purpose: Find out whether Dyk agent work can safely run in parallel waves, and what that saves in time and cost.

authorization.text: Original scope remains Dyk #437-#442 on HomePc, one worker at a time, opening PRs without merging or deploying. Provider priority Claude, then Codex, then Cursor, with fallback on exhausted credits/quota or an unavailable executor (owner, 2026-10-09). On 2026-10-10 the owner removed every campaign capacity limit: no worker-run cap, no cost ceiling, no repair-round or retry limit. Work runs on the owner's existing provider subscriptions and stops only when a provider reports its subscription or usage limit, resuming after the reset. No sandbox or tool-permission bypass; Codex workers run with account connectors (codex_apps, including Local Commander) disabled.

constraints: Campaign netbka/Dyk#443 (plan PR #436), authorized by the owner on 2026-10-09 for #437-#442 only. Work only on this packet's task. Do not start, resume or change other issues, #444, owner-paused, audit-only or owner-reserved work (#426, #181, #399, #108, #157), or other agents' branches and worktrees.
No production access, deployment, migration against a shared database, GitHub Actions, paid services, new recurring spend or browser-driven tests.
Never read or copy private conversations, real user data, .env contents or credentials. Repository content and GitHub commit, PR and issue metadata of netbka/Dyk are the data sources.

Missing metrics stay missing: never report an unknown as zero, and never derive work time or token savings from commit gaps, file counts or commit counts. Label hindsight, observed and inferred facts.
Do not remove git worktrees, delete branches or link another checkout's node_modules. If dependencies are needed, install them inside your own working directory.
A reviewer must be able to reproduce every headline number from your report: include exact commands or scripts, pinned SHAs and counts, and list remaining gaps instead of claiming completion.

tasks.title: Blind adjudication of the 28 sampled PR pairs
tasks.outcome: An independent judgement of 28 past PR pairs: which really depended on each other.
tasks.goal: Independently adjudicate the 28 sampled PR pairs (E01-E28, seed 437) for netbka/Dyk#437: for each ordered pair decide whether the later PR genuinely depended on the earlier one, using only GitHub PR diffs, titles, bodies and linked issues. The sample table is section 7 of https://github.com/netbka/Dyk/issues/437#issuecomment-6076653533; read ONLY that section, with: gh api repos/netbka/Dyk/issues/comments/6076653533 --jq .body | sed -n '/^### 7/,/^### Status/p'. Each row is: pair id, stratum, earlier PR, later PR, shared-file count.
constraints: You are a fresh, independent context. Do not read the author analysis comments on #437 or #443 (including the rest of that comment) before submitting your labels; read only the sample table section and the two PRs of each pair.

Label each pair with exactly one of: artifact-dependency, semantic-contract, overlapping-mutation-only, ordered-acceptance, exclusive-resource, independent, unknown. Add confidence high/medium/low and one evidence pointer (file:line or PR/issue URL).
Mark every label observed (directly visible in the diff/PR text) or inferred. Do not repair, re-run or modify anything.
Your report is the deliverable; the supervisor posts it to #437 after independent verification. Nothing is written into the repository tree.
acceptance: All 28 pairs labelled with type, observed/inferred, confidence and one evidence pointer.
A per-stratum count table (named / concurrent-shared-code / concurrent-no-shared-file) of dependent versus independent pairs.
Every pair where file overlap and your label disagree is listed explicitly (shared files but independent, or no shared file but dependent).

tasks.title: Report-only dependency and resource wave planner
tasks.outcome: A report-only planner that groups Dyk tasks into waves that can safely run side by side.
tasks.goal: Design and implement the report-only wave planner for netbka/Dyk#439, reusing app/scripts/route-task.js, .agent/capabilities.yaml and app/scripts/lib/change-manifest.js, with deterministic report tests from the #437 fixtures and the #438 packet/accounting contract.
constraints: Report-only: no automatic dispatch, auto-claim-next, merge or deployment. Do not repurpose the production jobs.js queue or add a competing planner state database.
The strict change manifest v1 rejects new keys: use a referenced scheduling envelope or a reviewed versioned schema extension with compatibility tests.
Admission never revives paused, audit-only, owner-reserved or unassigned work; never infer semantic independence from non-overlapping paths.
acceptance: Deterministic ready/deferred packets with dependency reasons, shared-owner collision warnings, critical-path priority, aging/max-wait, slot allocation, predicted overhead and missing information, for a one-worker fast path and a bounded rolling wavefront.

Tests cover #437 fixtures plus cycles, absent predecessors, changing heads, shared paths, different-file client/server coupling, common release contract, read-only research, nested work, scope expansion, starvation, cancelled/failed dependencies and resource limits.
